`parseDigits` returns `NaN` (the number `NaN`, not a string) when the input contains no parseable digits.

Reason: `parseInt(str, 10)` is `NaN`, so it falls into the fallback branch, sets `value = ""`, the loop appends nothing (no Han decimal chars, no UTF-16 digit ranges match), and it ends with `parseInt("", 10)`, which is `NaN`. It only returns a number when the fallback loop actually accumulated digits, e.g. `parseDigits("一") === 1`.

It returns the array `[null, {}]`: the first element is the failed `String.prototype.match` result (`null`), and the second element is an empty object (no token values were parsed). The matching branch instead returns `[matches, all]` with the raw match array and the deserialized token values.

Fixed. Root cause: `Interval.fromISO` parsed both halves as DateTimes unconditionally, so for the valid `<start>/<duration>` and `<duration>/<end>` forms the duration half made `DateTime.fromISO` throw `InvalidDateTimeError` under `Settings.throwOnInvalid`, escaping before the duration branch or the `Interval.invalid(...)` fallback could run. Now each half's parse is guarded (a throw/invalid parse just marks that half as "not a DateTime"), so duration-based intervals parse fine and genuinely unparsable input falls through to `Interval.invalid("unparsable", ...)`, which throws `InvalidIntervalError` when `throwOnInvalid` is set. Verified with the interval tests (127 pass), a temporary test named `Interval.fromISO works with Settings.throwOnInvalid` (passes), and the full suite (892 passed, 2 pre-existing failures in `toFormat.test.js` from a Node/ICU version difference — unchanged before and after).

It resets the internal `defaultZone` to `null` (`if (!z) { defaultZone = null; } else { defaultZone = normalizeZone(z); }`). So `Settings.defaultZoneName = ""` clears any previously set default zone, and `Settings.defaultZone` then falls back to `LocalZone.instance`.

Fixed. Root cause: `objToLocalTS()` in `src/impl/util.js` corrected years 0–99 with `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, which first normalized out-of-range month/day overflow inside the 19xx year and only then changed the year. Since 19xx leap status can differ from the target year's (2000 is leap, year 100 is not), dates passing through February were off by a day — e.g. `0099-12-31` + 61 days gave `0100-03-01` instead of `0100-03-02`. The fix sets year, month and day together (`d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`) so overflow normalizes under the target year's own leap rules. Verified: a temporary test of the reported shape fails before and passes after; a 282k-case differential test against an independent reference implementation shows 0 mismatches; full suite is 892 passed / 2 failed, byte-identical to the pre-fix baseline (the 2 failures are pre-existing ICU/Node-version French hour-padding issues in `toFormat.test.js`).

It's an abstract getter: it throws `ZoneIsAbstractError` (the base `Zone` class is an interface — every accessor/method on it throws that error, and concrete subclasses like `FixedOffsetZone`, `IANAZone`, `LocalZone` override it).

It returns a `FixedOffsetZone` built from that value: `zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` (the `Z` token's deserializer already converts the offset text to a number of minutes). `dateTimeFromMatches` returns the pair `[vals, zone]`, so the zone element is that `FixedOffsetZone`. (If `Z` is undefined it falls back to `IANAZone.create(matches.z)` when `z` is defined, otherwise `null`.)

Fixed. Root cause: `padStart` in `src/impl/util.js` compared `input.toString().length < n`, so the minus sign counted as a digit — year -100 produced `-100-01-01`, year -1 produced `00-1-01-01`. The fix strips the sign, pads the digits, and re-attaches it (keeping the original length guard so long years are never truncated): -100 → `-0100-01-01`, -1 → `-0001-01-01`, -118040 still `-118040-01-01`. Verified with a temporary test named `DateTime#toISODate() correctly pads negative years` (passes) and the full suite: 892 passed / 2 failed, identical to the pre-fix baseline (the 2 failures are the pre-existing French hour-padding ones).

`'narrow'`, `'short'`, or `'techie'` — returning `'+6'`, `'+06:00'`, or `'+0600'` respectively (per the docstring in `src/zone.js`; the concrete zones implement these).

Fixed. Root cause: `FixedOffsetZone.isValid` was hardcoded to `return true`, so `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")` / `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` reported a valid zone with a NaN offset, and since DateTime gates invalidity on `!zone.isValid`, DateTimes in such zones stayed valid. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`, so a non-numeric offset yields an invalid zone and any DateTime built in it is invalid ("unsupported zone"). Verified with temporary tests named `A DateTime in an invalid FixedOffsetZone is itself invalid` and `FixedOffsetZone is invalid when constructed with a non-numeric offset` (both pass) and the full suite: 892 passed / 2 failed, identical to the pre-fix baseline.

Fixed. Root cause: the conversion matrices in `src/duration.js` were incomplete — `casualMatrix.years` was missing `quarters: 4`, `casualMatrix.quarters` was missing `seconds: 91*24*60*60`, and `accurateMatrix.years` was missing `quarters: 4`. Since both `convert()` and `shiftTo()` index every ordered unit pair, those pairs produced NaN (e.g. `Duration.fromObject({years:1}).shiftTo("quarters")` → `{quarters: null}`). Added the three missing entries (values per the documented tables in `docs/math.md`). Verified all 36 ordered unit pairs for both `casual` and `longterm` accuracy: shiftTo/as/normalize round-trips all correct, no NaN; duration tests 114/114 pass; full suite 892 passed / 2 failed, identical to baseline.

Fixed. Root cause: `DateTime#isInDST()` compared the current offset with probes built via `this.set({ month: 1 })` / `this.set({ month: 5 })`, and `set()` keeps the day of month — so for a 1974 date with day ≥ 6 the "January" probe landed inside the 1974 year-round-DST window (Jan 6 – Oct 27) and returned the same offset, making `isInDST()` false. The January probe is now pinned to `set({ month: 1, day: 1 })`, a genuine standard-time reference. Verified: a full 1974 scan in America/New_York reports DST exactly Jan 6 – Oct 26, a 1248-sample cross-check against an independent reference across 13 zones × 8 years shows 0 mismatches, and the full suite is 892 passed / 2 failed — identical to the pre-fix baseline.
